feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with a clear senior digital communications profile and a logical career progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows breadth across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, tighter formatting consistency, and a few wording/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital communications, strategy, and platform leadership.  
- Strong credibility: long progression within one organization suggests trust, promotion, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good skills coverage: technical, strategic, editorial, and multimedia capabilities are all well represented and relevant.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes; include metrics tied to growth, engagement, efficiency, revenue, campaign performance, or team impact.  
- Fix writing/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; add the serial comma consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “content operations and enterprise web improvement” reads awkwardly.  
- Improve structure and style: there is overlap between Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidate to reduce repetition. Also standardize punctuation in bullets/hyphenation (e.g., cross-channel/multi-channel, front-end, organization-wide) and consider changing “Coleman DAVIS” to standard title case for consistency.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that signal public-sector/advocacy relevance without repeating the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and lead with the current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter summary of scope and leadership impact.
- Add sector context such as “mission-driven membership and advocacy organizations” to better match the NACo experience.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in platform modernization, digital governance, and workflow design that improves coordination across complex teams. Strong in stakeholder engagement, advocacy messaging, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid adding tool names or channel-by-channel detail here; those are already covered elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Cross-functional stakeholder coordination,” “Advocacy and policy communications.”
- Replace lower-level or redundant items with more strategic ones, e.g. swap “Web & CMS administration” for “CMS modernization & web governance.”
- Reduce overlap with Topline Skills by focusing this section on broad capability areas, not tools or execution details.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • CMS modernization & web governance • Editorial workflow & content operations • Multi-channel communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeat ideas already covered in the header and Soft Skills.
- “Web & CMS administration” overlaps with both Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the prior NACo positions and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic advisory value, and only the newest work not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, web governance, campaign architecture, and content operations for enterprise communications platforms.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine “digital systems, workflows and analytics” with governance/usability into one outcome-focused bullet.
- Separate 2–3 distinct contributions only: Drupal campaign/microsite builds; enterprise CMS/front-end troubleshooting; AI-enabled search strategy and structured content design.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, reduced publishing time, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics…” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Drupal microsites, AI search, and campaign storytelling also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and if channel oversight translated into clearer outcomes, not just responsibilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with an outcome-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and multi-channel communications for a national membership organization.”
- Tighten and prioritize the biggest wins: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build should lead the bullets.
- Add measurable results where possible for email/social/video: open rates, audience growth, production volume, cost savings, turnaround time, or reduced vendor spend.
- Consider a cleaner version:
- Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, events and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery to improve reporting and decision-making.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears in the current consultant role; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, repeatability, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show outcome: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and execution.” Add metrics if available (open rates, production volume, turnaround time, audience growth).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.
- “Publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” also appear in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating governance language verbatim.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the highest-value leadership areas and use tighter phrasing aligned to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector advocacy messaging & stakeholder communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for a more current, operational tone.
- Add one more specific systems/operations phrase if space allows; this candidate’s recent experience is strongest in governance, modernization, and organization-wide coordination.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid broad terms like “leadership” unless paired with a concrete scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; consider varying one of them.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths by leading with Drupal, CMS modernization, and AI-enabled search; move WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages later or drop one if space is tight.
- Replace “technical execution” list style with grouped terms to improve scanability and reduce repetition.
- If accurate, consider adding one impact cue in adjacent experience instead of here, e.g., tie Drupal to the 10,000+ page migration rather than naming multiple CMSs.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT” (Web Platforms & CMS; Coding & Technical Implementation; Automation & Workflow Systems).
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and recent project content.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and executive-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace weaker terms with impact-oriented language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent-profile CV, this item should signal depth or specialization, not just name tools.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and prioritize by strength/relevance: “Drupal (enterprise migration, governance, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/context instead of a plain list: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not materially important to recent work; it reads lighter than the rest.
- If you want more impact, align with proven outcomes from recent roles, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)”—but only if your CV format allows brief qualifiers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Avoid repeating CMS modernization here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & Technical Implementation:** JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop versioned/basic terms like **HTML5/CSS3** unless required by the role; they add little at this level.
- Consider grouping by function for clarity: **Front-end:** JavaScript, HTML/CSS | **Integration & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions | **Tagging:** Google Tag Manager
- If accurate, add scope/strength via modifiers such as **custom front-end implementation**, **serverless scripting**, or **deployment automation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already appear in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- **jQuery** may date the profile unless it reflects current, relevant work.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal actual systems leadership rather than basic familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and prioritize higher-value tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana | Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Remove lower-signal or older PM tools unless heavily used: Basecamp, Trello.
- Rename for stronger positioning: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools.”
- If accurate, add a qualifier to show depth: “Built and managed workflows in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; coordinated delivery in Jira and Asana.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same wording.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep only if they were central to cross-team operations.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and misses the scale/ownership already shown in recent NACo roles. Tightening the label and ordering by strongest/recent platform use would make it feel more intentional.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: “Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp” if Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform; otherwise put the main system first.
- Consider a clearer title: “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms” or “Email, Marketing Automation & Community Platforms.”
- If space allows, add light functional context instead of only brand names: “Higher Logic (member email/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation) • Mailchimp (campaign email).”
- Keep this item platform-focused; let the work experience carry audience size, newsletter volume, and channel leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple NACo bullets about email/newsletters; avoid adding impact claims here unless they’re removed elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the wording is broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make this entry more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content production, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Tighten scope and action: “Improved workflows across web, email, social and multimedia; supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video content.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics if available: number of livestreams, frequency/audience of video updates, site traffic impact, or turnaround improvements.
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped onboard and guide…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update” entry; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Workflow and cross-channel language also appears in 2018–2024 roles; keep this item focused on foundational setup and production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy, member engagement, or program visibility.
- Consider a stronger action/result version: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, creating a new multimedia channel for program and policy storytelling.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general coordination; later entries already show progression in cross-team operations and digital leadership.
